decisions.executionNote: Begin a continuous elbow-up right-arm approach to the right end of the set square; left arm stays at origin. Small forward motion and downward wrist pitch.
Prepare two closed fingertip contacts behind the set square, one in each workspace, to slide it flat without lifting any blocks. Gradually pitch downward and approach symmetrically.
Continue both wrists downward and inward to separated pushing points, keeping the square and all blocks on the tabletop.
Continue controlled approach; fingertip pushing locations are outside the blocks' span so the rail, not the grippers, will contact the cubes.
Bring fingertips toward vertical behind the rail, with a slight right-wrist height margin to avoid pressing into the table. Left contact is still approaching.
Square shifted slightly during approach. Finish near-vertical contacts with extra table clearance, pausing right translation while the left catches up behind the rail.
Finish the left vertical orientation and gently advance the right contact to straighten the rail's skew before a common forward push. Watch for actual rail motion.
The right advance did not move the rail. Reposition both closed tips behind its near edge with slight lift for clearance, then establish a lower pushing contact.
Lower closed fingertips behind the set square in small increments, maintaining vertical wrists and avoiding cube contact.
Close the gaps behind the skewed square at fixed height; left advances farther to establish matched rear-edge contacts before sweeping the cubes.
Advance both closed rear-edge contacts together at constant height. The nearer right side should move first and reduce the square's yaw before block contact.
The rail is now nearly horizontal with both rear contacts engaged. Slide it straight forward at fixed height toward the staggered blocks.
Maintain the flat synchronized sweep. The nearest cube has begun sliding; advance to collect the two farther cubes against the same straight edge.
All three cubes are now near the edge. Continue a short slow sweep to seat their faces against it, with a small right-side correction to level the row.
A final short, level seating push should remove the middle cube's remaining yaw. Then withdraw without moving the aligned row and reset both arms.
All three cubes now appear seated in a straight parallel row. Withdraw backward and slightly upward from the square without grasping it; begin the origin reset.
Row remains aligned after release. Open the clear grippers and retract both arms toward their original poses, smoothly undoing wrist pitch within the same elbow-up branch.
Continue the smooth bilateral reset away from the square, keeping the aligned cubes undisturbed and both elbows on the established branch.
Continue retreating and restoring the initial wrist attitude. The set square and all three aligned cubes remain stationary.
Restore both arms toward their starting positions and orientations while preserving configuration continuity; the tabletop row remains aligned.
Slow the final reset approach to the original arm poses, leaving the completed row undisturbed.
